title: Stop tying settings that don't imply that something should be on a Google indexed directory as such

labels.name: S-Tolerable
labels.description: Minor significance, cosmetic issues, low or no impact to users.

labels.name: T-Enhancement
labels.description: New features, changes in functionality, improvements in performance, or user-facing enhancements.

labels.name: O-Occasional
labels.description: Affects or can be seen by some users regularly or most users rarely

body:
### Description

I noticed having a space on matrix.org there is a very counter-intuitive result from the following settings: I have set the space's "Visibility" set to "Public", which to me means guests can join. A "History" setting isn't shown in Element. I also enabled the "Preview" setting, which I expect to allow people to see on [matrix.to](https://matrix.to) what the space's name and description is and nothing more.

All the above somehow implies *with all account names and handles joined fully leaked into the Google index* (uhm, what?).

**I didn't ever set some "[Add to] Public Directory Listing" setting where I expect no privacy for anyone joining**, I just want people to see the **a preview** on `matrix.to`.

Therefore, please add a separate "Public Directory Listing" setting instead, linking other related settings like this is just weird. This also concerns setting a regular room's "History" to "Anyone" for previews: I've also approached multiple channel owners on this to ask them to change it and only 1 out of around 10 wasn't extremely surprised. You should make it separate.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a room or space
2. Enable previewing by either setting "Preview" to on (space) or "History" to "Anyone" (room) for visitors on [matrix.to](https://matrix.to) 
3. Observe there is no ability now to not be thrown into a public directory and be Google-indexed, even though this really should be a separate setting
